We need to use integration by parts. We'll work out the indefinite integral first, and then proceed to work out the definite integral.

In this case, we define

$$
\begin{aligned}u=3{x}^{2}\, & ⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=6x \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)\, & ⟹\,v=\int \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x=\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x=\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the formula for integration by parts, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 3{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =(3{x}^{2})(\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{2})-\int (\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{2})(6x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{2}-3{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}x\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Again, we use integration by parts to evaluate $\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x.$ We take

$$
\begin{aligned}u=x & \,⟹\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,, \\ \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x) & \,⟹\,v=\int \operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\text{d}x=-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

In this case, the formula for integration by parts gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x & =\int u\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =uv-\int v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =x(-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2})-\int (-\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2})\cdot 1\,dx \\  & =-\frac{x\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2}+\frac{1}{2}\int \operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)\,dx \\  & =-\frac{x\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2}+\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{4}+D\end{aligned}
$$

where $D$ is an integral constant. 

So, we get that the indefinite integral is

$$
\begin{aligned}\int 3{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x & =\frac{3{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{2}-3\int x\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{2}-3(-\frac{x\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2}+\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{4}+D) \\  & =\frac{3{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{2}+\frac{3x\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2}-\frac{3\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{4}+C\end{aligned}
$$

where $C=-3D.$ Finally then, we can work out the definite integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}3{x}^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)\,\text{d}x & ={[\frac{3{x}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{2}+\frac{3x\operatorname{cos}⁡(2x)}{2}-\frac{3\operatorname{sin}⁡(2x)}{4}]}_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =\frac{3{(\frac{\pi }{2})}^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )}{2}+\frac{3(\frac{\pi }{2})\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )}{2}-\frac{3\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi )}{4}-(\frac{3(0)^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)}{2}+\frac{3(0)\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)}{2}-\frac{3\operatorname{sin}⁡(0)}{4}) \\  & =0+\frac{3\pi (-1)}{4}-0-0 \\  & =-\frac{3\pi }{4}\end{aligned}
$$
